 Print Winter vacation 2026-27: Delhi, UP, Haryana and other states' school holiday calendar School Winter Vacation 2026-27 : Schools across North India are expected to observe winter vacations during the 2026-27 academic session, with most states scheduling breaks between late December 2026 and mid-January 2027. However, the duration differs across states, depending on regional weather conditions, education department guidelines and school calendars. While schools in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Bihar generally follow shorter winter breaks, institutions in Himalayan regions observe longer holidays because of falling temperatures and snowfall. Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh have some of the longest winter vacation periods. School winter vacation 2026-27: State-wise schedule The following schedule outlines the reported and tentative winter vacation dates and reopening timelines across selected North Indian states and Union Territories. State/UT Winter vacation Reopening date 
 Uttar Pradesh December 31, 2026 to January 14, 2027 January 15, 2027 
 Delhi January 1 to January 15, 2027 January 16, 2027 
 Haryana January 1 to January 15, 2027 January 16, 2027 
 Rajasthan December 31, 2026 to January 10, 2027 January 11, 2027 
 Bihar December 25 to December 31, 2026 January 1, 2027 
 Punjab December 22 to December 31, 2026 (tentative) January 1, 2027 (tentative) 
 Jammu and Kashmir December 7, 2026 to February 28, 2027 (up to Class 8); December 14, 2026 to February 21, 2027 (Classes 9 to 12) March 1, 2027 (up to Class 8); February 22, 2027 (Classes 9 to 12) 
 Himachal Pradesh December 24 to December 31, 2026 (lower areas); January 1 to February 9, 2027 (winter-closing areas) Varies by zone 
 State-wise holiday details In Uttar Pradesh, the winter break is scheduled for 15 days, covering Basic Shiksha Parishad and recognised schools. Private institutions may follow different calendars. Delhi and Haryana have a 15-day vacation planned from January 1 to January 15, with schools scheduled to reopen on January 16. Rajasthan's holiday schedule follows the state education department's Shivira Panchang calendar. Bihar has a seven-day winter break, although authorities may extend the closure in January if cold-wave conditions persist. Punjab's schedule remains tentative, with extensions possible depending on temperatures. In Jammu and Kashmir, vacation periods differ according to class levels. Himachal Pradesh follows separate arrangements for lower and winter-closing areas, with extended breaks in high-altitude and snowbound regions.  District administrations and education departments may revise holiday schedules or change school timings during January because of severe cold, dense fog and high pollution levels. Private schools affiliated with CBSE, CISCE and international boards generally follow their institutional calendars. Many schedule Christmas and New Year breaks from December 24 or 25 until early January. States such as Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala generally have shorter Christmas and New Year holidays rather than extended winter vacations. Parents and students should check official school circulars for confirmed dates and reopening instructions.
